editorial:
Imagine coming home after a long, tiring day at work and just wanting to sink into your bed. That is exactly where you meet Aya, a young woman living on her own for the first time. As she rests, the movie takes you on a trip down memory lane. You get to see her childhood, the sadness of her mother moving away for work, and the sweet moment her dad brought home a cat named Mii-san to cheer her up. It feels like a warm hug and a sad sigh at the same time, focusing on the small, quiet moments that make a family feel real.

What really makes this shine is the art. Every single frame looks like a painting, from the sunlight hitting the floor to the city lights at night. It is a slow burn, so if you want a loud action movie, this isn't it. However, if you enjoy emotional stories that make you think about your own life, you will love it. Since the visuals are the best part, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection to see every detail clearly.
endingExplained: The story ends with a heartbreaking phone call. Aya learns that her father has passed away suddenly. The movie shows how the family cat, Mii-san, was the one constant bond between her and her dad. By the end, you realize the movie is about the pain of loss and the love that stays behind. It wraps up with Aya accepting the sadness while remembering the comfort her father and the cat gave her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves beautiful art and stories about family bonds.
